Sorry if this has been brought up before, but does Voat have any options to combat abusive mods?

Atko has said that he is working on public moderation logs, and the first step of this is in place already... go to voat.co/v/(verse name)/modlog/deleted. I have heard that a couple of subs have created their own public moderation logs but haven't seen them. I created a public log on my own sub, /v/omaha, but it has the downfall of being created and maintained by me, so the truth of it will - and should - always be suspect.

There is indeed a 10 sub limit for mods.

What hasn't been stated (from what I've seen, it may be in an old post somewhere) is whether @Atko is willing to step in in the event of an abusive mod. Of course, there will inevitably be a debate about whether the speech freedoms we enjoy here are inherent to the users or the the mods of each sub, and whether it would be right for Atko to step in. There have been discussion along the lines you suggest - voting systems and such - but I don't think any decisions have been made, and nothing has been instituted.

Regarding mod and username squatters, this has without a doubt happened. Atko has been very gracious in transferring ownership of subs that have sat empty with inactive moderators, so those who came over to squat mods have lost them. I have also seen on at least one occasion where someone squatted somebody's reddit username here on Voat, and when the owner of the reddit username proved who they were, the Voat username was given back to them... it was stated then that events like this will be handled on a case-by-case basis.
